2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal; in short, are that the petitioners herein being plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 99 of 2008 in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Dinajpur for declaration of Title and recovery of Khas possession impleading therein the opposite party No. 1 as the principal defendant and the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 as the proforma defendants. Late father and predecessor-in interest of the petitioners and the opposite party respondent Nos. 2 and 3 Alhaj Manjur Ali had been owning and possessing the suit land along with other landed property. During his life time he executed a Wasiyatnama' on 3.6.2004 before a Notary Public in Dinajpur with the consent of the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 and in presence of his relatives. The said 'Wasiyatnama' was duly authenticated by the said Notary Public. Late father of the petitioners and opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 allotted his property in favour of petitioners and opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 describing the sharers of each of them in different schedule. In pursuance of the said 'Wasiyatnama' the petitioners and the opposite parties amicably partitioned the schedule properties. After the death of Alhaj Mansur Ali on 23.6.2004 said opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 instituted the Other Suit No. 53 of 2006 for a declaration that 'Wasiyatnama' executed   by their father is false, fabricated and not binding upon them. Aforesaid Other Suit No. 53 of 2006 is pending in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Dinajpur, which have been contesting by the petitioners herein. Opposite Party No. 3 constructed 10 to 15 pucca shop rooms and enjoying the same through tenants. The opposite party No. 2 transferred 14 decimals of land by a registered kabala dated 25.10.2005 in favour of the petitioners from his share. The opposite party No. 2 executed a sale deed in favour of the petitioners in respect of aforesaid 14 decimals of land. In this way the petitioners and the opposite parties are enjoying the possession of the suit property by amicable partition. 

 3. After institution of the aforesaid suit for declaration and for recovery of khas possession the petitioners filed an application for temporary injunction on the averments made in the plaint before the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dinajpur, who was pleased to reject the application for temporary injunction by his judgment and order dated 6.4.2009.
